text: Existential dread for several months, especially at night. I'd lie awake thinking about the end of everything. Mild depersonalisation, like I was watching myself from a distance.
Ein paar Tage neben mir gestanden, dann war alles gut.

Everything got worse. My PTSD symptoms, which had been bad, became much worse. Before, I had nightmares maybe twice a week. After, it was every night, and now the basement and the park were in them too, mixed with Afghanistan. I started sleeping with a knife under my pillow, which my wife found and that scared her a lot. I couldn't be in dark rooms with candles, couldn't hear drumming or any kind of rhythmic banging without going into fight mode.

The hypervigilance was off the charts. I'd scan every room, sit with my back to the wall, check the locks five times every night. I couldn't drive because every car behind me felt like a threat. I had several episodes where I lost time, I'd 'come to' somewhere without knowing how I got there.

The guilt about hurting that guy was eating me alive. I kept thinking that I'm dangerous, that I shouldn't be around people, especially my kids. I moved into the spare room. I avoided my kids because I was afraid I might hurt them during a flashback. That was the worst part. My daughter was six and she didn't understand why daddy didn't want to play.

I started drinking heavily to get to sleep. I'd been mostly sober for two years before that. Within a couple of months I was drinking a bottle of whiskey a day.

I became deeply depressed. I stopped going out, stopped answering my buddies, stopped showering. I thought about suicide a lot. I had a plan. The only thing that stopped me was my kids.

I also got very angry, at the guy, at the VA for making me wait so long, at myself. I'd punch walls. I broke my hand once.

This went on for about a year and a half before things started to change.

Afterimages and trails that have lasted for 3 years now. Static in dark rooms. I was really anxious about it at first and thought I'd damaged my brain. I'm less anxious about it now but the visuals are still there every day.

Ich hatte monatelang das Gefühl, nicht wirklich zu existieren. Ich habe mich im Spiegel angeschaut und mich gefragt, wer das ist. Die Angst, dass ich allein im Universum bin und alles nur eine Illusion ist, kam immer wieder, vor allem nachts. Ich habe mein Studium für ein Semester unterbrochen, weil ich mich nicht konzentrieren konnte. Ich hatte auch Phasen von Depression, in denen ich nicht aus dem Bett gekommen bin. Mittlerweile, nach zwei Jahren, geht es mir viel besser. Ich glaube, die Erfahrung hat mich gezwungen, mich mit Fragen auseinanderzusetzen, die ich vorher verdrängt habe, und ich bin heute bescheidener und dankbarer, dass es andere Menschen gibt.
Nightmares about snakes for a few months, then it faded. I think in the end it taught me something about my own fear and about not trusting groups blindly.

Seitdem habe ich Angst, dass so etwas wieder passiert, auch ohne dass ich etwas genommen habe. In Meetings habe ich manchmal Panikattacken und das Gefühl, alle schauen mich an. Ich habe mit dem Microdosing aufgehört.

For over a year I couldn't shake the feeling that the world is a simulation and that I'm the only real person. I knew intellectually that this was not true, but emotionally it felt true all the time. People seemed like scripts. Conversations felt like I was playing a game. I had strong derealisation, the world looked too bright and too sharp and flat, like a video game render.

I became very depressed. If nothing was real, nothing mattered, so I stopped caring about my studies, my friends, my future. I failed several courses. My girlfriend broke up with me because she said I was treating her like she wasn't there, which, in a way, was true.

I developed intrusive thoughts, little phrases that would pop up: 'this isn't real', 'you're alone', 'they're laughing at you'. They would come dozens of times a day. I would look for 'glitches' everywhere, like déjà vu or coincidences, and every time I found one it would send me into a panic.

I also had trouble sleeping because I was afraid that when I fell asleep I would wake up in the machine room again.

It's been almost three years. The derealisation is much less now, most days I feel the world is real. The thoughts still come but not so often.

Afterwards I had anxiety in hot weather and when I felt thirsty, some health anxiety. But I also came away with a sense that my ancestors were with me, and a respect for life and for my body that I didn't have before.

Nach der Erfahrung bin ich in eine tiefe Depression gefallen. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass etwas in mir kaputtgegangen ist. Ich konnte mich über nichts mehr freuen und habe mich von allen zurückgezogen. Ich hatte ständig Angst, dass ich verrückt werde, und oft das Gefühl, dass die Welt nicht echt ist. Ich habe mein Studium abgebrochen und bin zu meinen Eltern zurückgezogen. Ich konnte monatelang kaum das Haus verlassen. Ich hatte auch Schlafstörungen und Konzentrationsprobleme, und ich habe mich für alles geschämt. Das hat sich über fast zwei Jahre hingezogen.
Grief came up afterwards, but it was healthy grief.

Nach dem Retreat kamen immer wieder Erinnerungen an meine Kindheit hoch, oft in Momenten, in denen ich nicht damit gerechnet habe. Ich war sehr reizbar und habe meinen Partner oft ohne Grund angeschrien. Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich Angst vor Nähe habe und mich zurückziehe, sobald jemand mir zu nahe kommt.
